content.text: By the end of this lesson, you should be able to:
Explain how inhibitors affect enzyme activity
Interpret graphs showing effects of inhibitors
Give examples of inhibitors and their uses

are molecules that reduce or stop enzyme activity. Understanding inhibition is important for understanding metabolism, drug action, and how cells regulate their chemistry. Inhibitors can be reversible or irreversible.
Inhibitor has similar shape to substrate
Can be overcome by increasing substrate concentration
Inhibitor binds to allosteric site (not active site)
Product of pathway inhibits early enzyme
Many drugs work by enzyme inhibition
They temporarily block the active site
Non-competitive inhibitors bind to the active site
They bind to a different (allosteric) site
Inhibitor competes with substrate for active site
Site other than active site where molecules bind
Product inhibits enzyme earlier in pathway
Competitive: inhibitor competes for active site; similar shape to substrate
Non-competitive: inhibitor binds elsewhere; changes enzyme shape
Competitive inhibition can be overcome by increasing [S]
Non-competitive inhibition cannot be overcome by increasing [S]
Many drugs work as enzyme inhibitors
